automaticJob.encryption: Existing RSA-4096 recipient public key only is provided to runner. AES-256-GCM encrypts streams before disk or upload, RSA-OAEP-SHA256 wraps fresh per-artifact key. Recovery key and recovery code never enter runner secrets or logs.
automaticJob.database: Owner-approved dedicated stackendbox_backup_reader login created without changing existing passwords. pg_read_all_data membership and BYPASSRLS enable protected Auth export. Storage metadata alone does not recover payloads. Concurrent object changes during export may require consistency reconciliation during recovery.

restoreOnNewComputer: Download private custody archive from the verified folder, verify archive SHA256 above, and unpack into a restricted local directory. Select a complete dated generation. Obtain the recovery code separately and store it in a temporary restricted file personally. Never share it in chat or logs.

Install official Node.js 24 and PostgreSQL 17 or compatible newer restore tools. Clone the existing repository and check out verified recovery tooling commit 69a118f on feature/cloudflare-workers-proof, which preserves baseline 6dc0c15. Run tools from the repository root. The five-file main backup-only release does not contain the full portal recovery tests. No original Windows identity or npm install is needed for the native Node portable-key SQL recovery drill.

On a new Windows computer, set POSTGRES_BIN to installed PostgreSQL bin, PORTAL_DRILL_ROOT to an isolated local work directory, PORTAL_RECOVERY_KEY_FILE to the downloaded portable-recovery-key.pem, and PORTAL_RECOVERY_CODE_FILE to the personally created separate code file. Run node scripts/portal-restore-drill.mjs followed by the selected generation directory. The drill restores only a fresh local database, never the live project.

New automated generations contain summary.json.enc. The updated drill decrypts it in memory, verifies the encrypted artifacts, decrypts database archive and checks RLS/integrity/persistence in the isolated local database. Existing manually uploaded generations retain their ordinary non-secret summary.json. Windows is the currently supported drill host. Linux/macOS full restore needs an equivalent reviewed script, not an invented claim of cross-platform acceptance.

Before disaster production restore, follow Supabase's current supported new-project migration instructions. Restore application records, Auth identities and hashes, memberships, assignments, RLS and migration history without overwriting existing production as a drill. Validate MFA and encrypted database material against the restored project's encryption configuration. The completed local SQL drill is not proof of a hosted Auth service disaster restore.

Restore storage buckets, access policies and actual object payloads using encrypted manifest bucket/path mappings. Verify checksums, access controls and client isolation. Current custody generation has zero payloads. Never claim future uploaded files are backed up before a successful object-inclusive generation exists.

Restore provider configuration separately, test public/client email separation, normal password recovery, administrator MFA, assigned domains and file access on an isolated hostname. Only then approve production DNS routing. Keep registrar writes and live payments disabled throughout recovery.
configurationAndSecretRecoverySeparate: Maintain private owner account-recovery methods for Supabase, Google Drive, GitHub, Cloudflare, Spaceship, Whop and Brevo, including MFA recovery custody. Do not store account recovery codes in the backup folder.

Record Supabase region, Auth Site URL/redirect allowlist, MFA policy, storage bucket/policy definitions, project encryption root material where applicable, custom-role credentials, extensions/publications, scheduled jobs and restore order. SQL records do not replace Auth service configuration or encryption-root recovery. Use Supabase's supported key migration process when encrypted Vault/column material is present.

Keep provider secret values in an owner-controlled separate trusted vault, never GitHub source or this report. Preserve distinct public BREVO_API_KEY and portal BREVO_CLIENT_API_KEY, primary Spaceship credentials, Sandbox Whop key/signing secret, Turnstile secret, backend bridge and scheduler credentials. Non-exportable hosted secrets need independently saved owner copies for disaster recovery.

Keep company-zone-before.json, company-zone-comparison.json, current DNSSEC transition state, Vercel deployment rollback ID, Worker routing/build profile and all eleven DNS values available. Public DNS keys and records are not the private recovery code.
No provider secrets, production DNS, live payments, registrar settings or customer records changed by the offsite custody upload or prepared automation.
